title: Find Peak Element
statement: A peak is an element strictly greater than its neighbours (treat the outside of the list as negative infinity). Adjacent elements are never equal. Return the index of any peak in O(log n). (The checker accepts any valid peak.)

hints.1_question: You don't need the highest peak, just any peak. If you stand at mid and look at its right neighbour, what does the slope tell you?
hints.2_nudge: If nums[mid] < nums[mid + 1] you are going uphill to the right, so a peak must exist on the right. Otherwise one exists at mid or on the left.
hints.3_big_hint: While lo < hi: mid; if nums[mid] < nums[mid+1]: lo = mid + 1 else hi = mid. Return lo.

known_bugs.name: returns the maximum value instead of an index
known_bugs.followup: The function should return an index. What does max() return?

known_bugs.name: lo = mid never makes progress
known_bugs.followup: With two elements left and an uphill slope, what are lo, mid and the new lo?

known_bugs.name: linear scan that never handles a peak at the end
known_bugs.followup: In a strictly increasing list, does your loop ever return? What should the answer be?

followups: Why is a peak guaranteed to exist on the uphill side?
